dct_description_sm: Beluga may be exposed to more stressors and contaminants as the environment changes globally and locally which requires ongoing monitoring. Since Inuvialuit lead subsistence lifestyles includes harvesting beluga whales, there are concerns about the health and contaminants levels. The purpose of this project is to determine contaminants levels in beluga and the overall health of the whales as well as establish baseline levels for future long term monitoring. The study site was chosen to compare the whales from Hendrickson Island with Paulatuk. The whales from Paulatuk are from the same population as those harvested in Hendrickson Island, but previous research  from 2005 showed differences in mercury concentrations, diet markers and other biological measurement. Indeed, the habitat near Paulatuk is very different than the Mackenzie Estuary also habitat is used differently and may reflect different diets ans processes among the whales.
dct_title_s: Paulatuk Beluga whales: Health and Knowledge
